packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-06 - unverified image-only reading

EXPOSURE / RULES
No proposed identification or prior reading was present in my context. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files of this packet. No web, search, catalogue or edition was used.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
Six images: image-001 = reduced overview of one face of a tall narrow parchment strip (about 5 cm wide by about 23 cm tall against the ruler in the photograph), with native tiles image-002 (upper half) and image-003 (lower half); image-004 = reduced overview of the other face, with tiles image-005 and image-006. The tiles overlap each other by a few lines.
The strip is upright; the script runs horizontally across the short dimension, so each line is only a fragment (a few words) of what was presumably a wider line; both left and right edges appear to be cuts through text.
Face A (image-001..003): single text block as far as visible, very pale brown cursive documentary-looking script, heavily abraded and stained. A large solid red rectangle (about 2.5 x 3 cm) occupies the upper left; it is opaque pigment with a scalloped edge, with no letter-form recognisable inside it (observation). Below it are five or six broad horizontal red bars spanning the strip's width at irregular intervals, each darker and thicker in its left third; lines of text lie between the bars. Red spatter and pale buff blotches (pigment loss or paste residue) are scattered across the face. A modern pencil number is written in the lower blank area. No running title, no column division, no interlinear gloss visible.
Tentative interpretation only: the red bars look like rulings or dividers separating short entries (two or three lines each), i.e. a list or register-like layout rather than continuous prose; the recurring "f." followed by minims in several lines looks like a repeated unit plus numeral. I cannot confirm this from the image.

FACE A - TRANSCRIPTION
Most of this face is not legibly recoverable from the images; what follows are the letter groups I could actually see. Line numbers count visible text lines from the top of each tile, bars not counted.

  -- red rectangle occupies the left two thirds of the next c. 8 line-heights; to its right only line-ends are visible:

  -- red bar --

  -- red bar --

  -- blank area; modern pencil numeral, reads "9114" or "944" followed by a stroke(?) --
  -- remainder of the strip blank or wholly abraded --
  -- red bar with a small red cross-like mark on it near the foot --

FACE B (image-004 overview; tiles image-005 upper, image-006 lower)
Layout (observation): the same strip turned over. The red rectangle and the red bars appear again at the mirrored positions (rectangle now upper right, bars now darker toward the right), so the red has soaked through the parchment or was applied to both faces; I cannot tell from the images which face carries the original pigment. Script as on face A: small pale-brown cursive, lines running across the short dimension; here the lines begin at the left with an enlarged looped capital (several look like "D", i.e. entries beginning "De"/"D...", tentative) set slightly into the left margin, which suggests the left edge of this face preserves line beginnings while the right edge is a cut. Entries of two to four lines are separated by the red bars. Grey smudging and creases obscure the centre.

  -- red bar --

image-006 line 19: [...]d(?)co(?) ca(?)c(?)lau9(?) . q(?)[...]
image-006 line 20: [blank or abraded]
image-006 line 21: [...]p(?)[..] [...] Sy(?)ne(?)d(?)ia(?)[...]
image-006 line 22: [...] c(?)[...]
image-006 line 23: [...] yn(?) Mak(?)ed(?)[...]
image-006 line 24: [...] f . z(?)oz(?) . t(?)[...]
image-006 line 25: [...]ali(?)[..] capud(?) [...]to(?)[...]
image-006 line 26: [blank or abraded]
image-006 line 27: [...]d(?)o he(?)m(?)[..] p(?)etri(?) h(?)[...]
image-006 line 28: f(?) . z(?) [...]
image-006 line 29: [...] t(?) m(?)o D(?)au(?)[...]
  -- red bar --
image-006 line 30: [...] [..]m(?)om(?) [...]  (cut at foot of strip)

SELECTION AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
I attempted every visible line on both faces. Nothing here amounts to connected text: no span of even three consecutive securely read words was obtained on either face. All letter groups above are low-confidence; treat none of them as a quotable reading. The comparatively firmest observations are (a) the recurring "f ." followed by a short numeral-like group in many entries on both faces (image-002 lines 9, 12, 15; image-005 line 17; image-006 lines 7, 10, 24, 28), (b) enlarged looped initials at entry heads on face B, (c) entries of two to four short lines divided by red bars.
Tentative interpretation: a list of short entries, each ending in "f." plus a number - compatible with either a table/index with references or an account/rental with sums (f. = an abbreviation for a unit); the image does not let me decide, and the language of the entries could not be established.

LIMITATIONS
- The strip is a narrow vertical cut; every line is truncated on at least one side.
- The ink is extremely faded to pale brown and overlaid by red pigment, buff blotches, grey smudges and creases; resolution of the tiles is adequate, the loss is in the leaf.
- The red rectangle hides the upper third of each face.
- Which face is recto and which is verso is not determinable.
- A raking-light, UV or multispectral image would be needed for a real reading; a wider view cannot help because the strip is complete in the overview.
- Unverified image reading.
